example: In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
The example `requirements.references.selector_impl_and_trait` gives a concrete case with expected outcomes. In `src/lib.rs`, `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`. `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`. `read` in a trait has `trait[Read]/fn[read]`.

Two tests carry `{test}` references to it:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` parses a source containing `struct Thing;`, `impl Thing { fn run() {} }`, `impl Trait for Thing { fn run() {} }` and `trait Trait { fn read(&self); ... }`, using the path `src/lib.rs`. It asserts that the parsed outline's selectors include `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`. It also asserts that each selector resolves back to a node carrying that same selector.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates]` makes the same three assertions on a similar source.

The helpers `outline` (which calls `parse` and panics on error) and `selectors` (which maps nodes to their selector strings) are straightforward, so the assertions test real parser output.

The tests name the trait `Trait` rather than `Read`. The selector form `trait[Name]/fn[method]` is the same, so this does not change what is checked. Both `run` methods appear in one file and get distinct selectors, which covers the inherent-versus-trait impl distinction the example describes. I found no gap.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
